title: Chiranjeevi Meets Amit Shah Over AI Deepfake Misuse, Seeks Stronger Protection for Artists
description: Chiranjeevi and Ram Charan met Amit Shah on November 2 to seek stronger safeguards against AI deepfakes. The government promised an urgent examination.
content: Megastar Chiranjeevi has taken his concerns over the growing misuse of artificial intelligence and deepfake technology directly to the Central Government. The Telugu film star, accompanied by his son and actor Ram Charan, met Union Home Minister Amit Shah in Hyderabad on November 2 and discussed the increasing threat posed by digitally manipulated videos and AI-generated content targeting artists and the entertainment industry. During the meeting, Chiranjeevi highlighted how artificial intelligence tools are increasingly being misused to create manipulated images, videos and other content without the consent of the individuals involved. He expressed concern that such practices could seriously damage an artist's reputation, personal dignity, professional identity and creative rights. Union Minister G. Kishan Reddy was also present during the meeting. Chiranjeevi and Ram Charan reportedly requested stronger legal safeguards and strict action against individuals who misuse AI technology to create or circulate objectionable and misleading content targeting artists. Following the meeting, Chiranjeevi shared details of the discussion through a social media post. He expressed gratitude to Amit Shah for listening to their concerns and said the Home Minister had assured them that the government would examine the issue urgently and work towards introducing stronger protections and strict penalties against those responsible for such misuse. Chiranjeevi also revealed that Amit Shah had advised them to submit a formal written representation explaining the concerns in detail. The Home Minister entrusted G. Kishan Reddy with coordinating the matter so that the issue could be examined further. The actor described the response as an encouraging development for the film fraternity and expressed hope that the discussion would eventually lead to meaningful protection for artists and their creative work. Ram Charan also shared photographs from the meeting and spoke about the importance of addressing the growing misuse of AI and deepfake technology. He said he was encouraged by the Home Minister's understanding of the concerns raised by the father-son duo and appreciated the assurance that the government would examine the matter urgently. Ram Charan emphasised that digitally manipulated content could have a serious impact not only on individual actors but also on the wider entertainment industry. He welcomed the government's willingness to consider stronger safeguards and strict action against those responsible for abusing these technologies. The meeting comes amid increasing concerns within the Indian entertainment industry over the misuse of artificial intelligence. Deepfake technology can digitally recreate a person's face, voice or appearance and place them in situations that never actually occurred. Although these tools have legitimate applications in filmmaking and creative production, their misuse can result in misleading, humiliating or damaging material being circulated online. Actors and other public figures are particularly vulnerable because their photographs, videos and voices are widely available online. Manipulated content can spread rapidly through social media platforms, making it difficult for victims to control its circulation or prevent further misuse. One widely discussed example involved actress Rashmika Mandanna, whose face was digitally inserted into a video that circulated online in 2023. The incident attracted widespread attention and renewed discussions about the dangers of deepfake technology. In January 2024, Delhi Police arrested Eemani Naveen, a 24-year-old engineering graduate from Andhra Pradesh, in connection with the creation and circulation of the manipulated video. The incident highlighted how easily artificial intelligence can be used to create misleading material involving real individuals. It also brought attention to the difficulties faced by victims who must deal with reputational damage, privacy concerns and the rapid spread of manipulated content. Chiranjeevi's latest meeting with Amit Shah has brought these concerns back into focus, particularly the need to protect the identity and dignity of people working in the entertainment industry. The issue extends beyond film actors and can affect singers, public personalities, content creators and other individuals whose images and voices can be digitally manipulated. The demand for stronger safeguards also raises questions about accountability. Artists and industry representatives are increasingly concerned about how victims can report deepfake material, how quickly harmful content can be removed and what penalties should apply to people who deliberately create or distribute such material without permission. The government has assured Chiranjeevi and Ram Charan that their concerns will be examined urgently. However, the meeting does not yet represent the announcement of a new law or a confirmed set of penalties. A formal written representation is expected to help communicate the concerns in greater detail before further steps are considered. For the film fraternity, the discussion represents an important effort to bring the issue of AI misuse and deepfakes to the attention of policymakers. As artificial intelligence technology continues to develop, protecting personal identity, creative ownership and individual dignity is becoming an increasingly important challenge. Chiranjeevi's meeting with Amit Shah has therefore placed the protection of artists against AI-generated manipulation firmly in the spotlight. The next steps will depend on the government's examination of the concerns and whether stronger safeguards and penalties can be introduced to address the growing threat of deepfake misuse in India. Sources: statements shared on social media by Chiranjeevi and Ram Charan, and reports by IANS, Outlook India, Gulf News and Free Press Journal.

title: Sonu Nigam Introduces 19-Year-Old Son Nevaan Nigam With Debut Short Film 'Slide'
description: Sonu Nigam introduced his 19-year-old son Nevaan's first project, the sci-fi short film Slide, with an emotional Diwali post about his hard work.
content: Singer Sonu Nigam has introduced his 19-year-old son, Nevaan Nigam, to audiences through Slide, a science-fiction short film that marks the young artist's first project of his own in music and filmmaking. The project was unveiled around Diwali, with Sonu and his wife Madhurima Nigam sharing the announcement through a joint social media post. In his message, Sonu reflected on his son's journey from a shy child to a young performer who has been working consistently to develop his musical and artistic abilities. The singer revealed that Nevaan was once hesitant to sing even in front of his own father, despite growing up in a family with a strong musical background. Sonu also spoke about the discipline Nevaan has developed over the years. According to the singer, his son practises vocal exercises taught by his coach for up to 16 hours a day and has completed one-take studio recordings with renowned music producer Poo Bear. Nevaan has also been spending hours practising dance to improve his performance skills. Recalling his son's early connection with music, Sonu mentioned that Nevaan recorded Kolaveri Di in a studio when he was just four years old. At around four and a half, he also performed his father's song Abhi Mujh Mein Kahin live on stage. Sonu acknowledged the affection audiences had shown Nevaan since those early appearances and requested their blessings as he begins a new chapter. The singer emphasised that Nevaan intends to explore his own creative direction rather than simply follow the musical path established by his father and grandfather. He wished his son a journey guided by dignity, hard work, passion and humility. Nevaan has also been in the public eye in recent years. In February 2025, he made his Instagram debut with a series of photographs showing his two-year physical transformation, and Sonu shared the post with a message of blessings. ## About Nevaan Nigam's Short Film Slide Slide combines music with a science-fiction storyline centred on a scientist who becomes stranded across different periods, ranging from the Wild West to the Disco Era. His journey takes an unexpected turn after he loses a special totem watch that works with his glove to operate a time-travel machine. As he navigates unfamiliar eras and unexpected situations, the scientist encounters a girl and takes her on an extraordinary journey through time. The song Slide accompanies their adventure as he introduces her to different wonders of the world. The short film has been directed by Alexander Cobian and Nevaan Nigam. Nevaan developed the concept, while the music was composed by The Audibles. The project serves as an introduction to his creative vision and his plans to explore music and visual storytelling. With Slide, Nevaan begins his journey in the entertainment world, carrying the influence of his family's musical legacy while attempting to establish an identity of his own. Sources: Sonu Nigam's Instagram post and a report by IANS.

title: Salman Khan Questions ₹4,000 Crore Ramayana Budget Talk, Says Focus Should Be on Ram, Sita and Ravana
description: Salman Khan says Ramayana should be discussed for its story, not its ₹4,000 crore budget, and recalls a Ramayana film he once shelved with his brother.
content: Bollywood actor Salman Khan has shared his views on the widespread discussion surrounding the reported ₹4,000 crore budget of Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana. The actor believes that conversations about the ambitious adaptation should focus on the epic's story, characters and cultural significance rather than being dominated by its production costs and visual effects. Speaking at the trailer launch of his upcoming film Maatrubhumi: May War Rest In Peace in Mumbai on November 6, Salman questioned the repeated attention given to the film's budget and VFX. He said that Ramayana deserves to be discussed for what it represents, particularly its central characters and the scriptures on which the epic is based. "I just think Ramayana should be discussed for Ramayana and not its VFX or its cost of production. I think this narrative that Rs 4,000 crore... VFX, VFX, I just don't think that is correct. Ramayana should be discussed for its characters, Ram, Ravana, Sita, on the scriptures," Salman said. The actor also spoke about the qualities associated with Lord Ram and drew a comparison with the character he portrays in Maatrubhumi, Colonel B. Santosh Babu. He described Ram as an ideal husband, son, father, brother and warrior, adding that his character in the upcoming film possesses similar qualities. Salman was also asked whether he had watched the new adaptation. In response, he mentioned that he had seen Ramanand Sagar's popular television version of Ramayana. ## Salman Recalls Shelved Ramayana Film With His Brother During the interaction, Salman revisited an interesting episode from his own career. He revealed that around 20 years ago, he and his brother, Sohail Khan, had planned to make a film based on Ramayana, with Salman expected to play Lord Ram. Recalling the incident, the actor said that after the project was announced, photographers captured him and his brother leaving a location late at night. He said the media subsequently portrayed them as Ram and Lakshman by placing crowns on their photographs. Salman recalled that the coverage became a talking point, and the project was eventually shelved. His comments offered a glimpse into an earlier attempt to bring the epic to the big screen that did not move forward. Media reports over the years have also described an earlier Ramayana project from the 1990s, directed by Sohail Khan, with Salman reportedly set to play Ram. According to reports, the exact reasons that film was shelved have never been officially confirmed, so the account above is Salman's own recollection. ## Ramayana's Reported Budget and Cast Directed by Nitesh Tiwari, Ramayana features Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Ram, Sai Pallavi as Sita and Yash as Ravana, with Sunny Deol also part of the cast. The first part, titled Ramayana: Rise of a Legend, was released on November 5, 2026, and reportedly crossed ₹100 crore in India within two days, according to figures from Sacnilk cited by media. The reported ₹4,000 crore figure has become a major talking point around the project. Reports describe it as the combined budget of the two-part saga, rather than the cost of the first instalment alone. ## Salman Khan's Maatrubhumi Release Date Salman's remarks came during the trailer launch of Maatrubhumi: May War Rest In Peace. The film is now set to release on December 4, 2026, after a delay. With his comments, Salman has urged audiences to look beyond the production scale of Ramayana and pay greater attention to the characters, values and story at the heart of the epic. Sources: reports by Free Press Journal, WION, Outlook India, Pinkvilla, Glamsham and India.com.

title: Katrina Kaif and Vicky Kaushal Reveal Son Vihaan's Face for the First Time on Diwali, Call It Their 'Brightest Diwali Yet'
description: Katrina Kaif and Vicky Kaushal shared the first clear photo of son Vihaan on Diwali, a day after his first birthday, calling it their brightest yet.
content: Bollywood actors Katrina Kaif and Vicky Kaushal made Diwali 2026 especially memorable for their family and fans by sharing the first clear public photograph of their son, Vihaan Kaushal. The couple posted a family picture on social media on November 8, giving followers their first proper glimpse of the little boy's face since his birth. Sharing the photograph, Katrina and Vicky described the occasion as their "brightest Diwali yet" and extended festive wishes to everyone. Their caption read, "Our brightest Diwali yet... Wishing everyone love, light and happiness. - Vicky, Katrina & Vihaan." The photograph features the couple posing with their son in coordinated traditional outfits. Katrina is dressed in a bright yellow embroidered ethnic suit, while Vicky wears an elegant cream-coloured traditional ensemble. Vihaan complements his parents in a cream kurta-pyjama paired with a yellow jacket. The toddler can be seen smiling and waving at the camera, making the family photograph a special moment for fans who had been waiting to see his face. Katrina and Vicky are seen sitting beside their son, sharing the festive moment together. ## Face Reveal Comes a Day After Vihaan's First Birthday The couple's Diwali post came just one day after Vihaan celebrated his first birthday on November 7, 2026. He was born on November 7, 2025, and the actors announced his arrival through a joint social media message expressing their happiness and gratitude. At the time, they wrote, "Our bundle of joy has arrived. With immense love and gratitude, we welcome our baby boy." In January 2026, the couple introduced their son by revealing his name, Vihaan Kaushal. They shared a photograph showing the baby's tiny hand held between their hands and described him as their ray of light. However, they had largely kept his face away from public view until the latest Diwali photograph. The decision to share his first clear public photograph has attracted considerable attention, with fans celebrating the special family occasion. ## Bollywood Celebrities React to the Family Photograph Several film personalities and friends from the entertainment industry responded to the couple's post with affectionate messages and festive wishes. Ananya Panday wrote "Oh my god !!!" in the comments, while Sonam Kapoor wished the family a happy Diwali. Kiara Advani dropped heart emojis, and Kareena Kapoor Khan affectionately called the little boy "Puddinggggg Baba". Karan Johar wished Vihaan a happy birthday, and other celebrities, including Arjun Kapoor, Mrunal Thakur, Malaika Arora and Huma Qureshi, also reacted to the post. The photograph quickly became a talking point among fans, who welcomed the rare glimpse of the couple's son and sent birthday and Diwali wishes to the family. ## Katrina Kaif and Vicky Kaushal's Journey as Parents Katrina Kaif and Vicky Kaushal married on December 9, 2021, in a private wedding ceremony at Six Senses Fort Barwara in Rajasthan. Since then, the actors have generally maintained a private approach towards their personal lives. Their son Vihaan's arrival in November 2025 marked a new chapter for the couple. Vicky has previously spoken about how fatherhood has changed his perspective, describing the experience as magical and explaining how watching his wife and child share happy moments has made him more sensitive and responsible. The couple's latest Diwali post offered fans a rare glimpse into their family life. With Vihaan celebrating his first birthday just a day before the festival, the photograph marked a particularly memorable occasion for the Kaushal family. Sources: the couple's Instagram post and reports by India TV, IANS, Outlook India, Free Press Journal and WION.

title: Priyanka Chopra Shares Diwali Family Album With Nick Jonas and Daughter Malti From Los Angeles
description: Priyanka Chopra shared photos of her Diwali in Los Angeles with Nick Jonas and daughter Malti, in festive outfits amid candles, flowers and warm lights.
content: Actor Priyanka Chopra Jonas gave fans a glimpse into her Diwali celebrations by sharing a collection of family photographs featuring her husband, American singer Nick Jonas, and their daughter, Malti Marie Chopra Jonas. The pictures, posted on November 8, 2026, captured the family's festive moments at their Los Angeles home. Sharing the photographs on Instagram, Priyanka wrote, "Some camera roll favourites from this Diwali. Wishing you all a very Happy Diwali." The post featured a mix of family pictures, festive decorations and candid moments from the celebrations. For the occasion, Priyanka chose a burgundy and gold traditional outfit featuring intricate embellishments, zardozi detailing, beadwork and gold-thread embroidery. She completed her look with statement gold earrings, matching bangles and a kundan maang tikka. Her hair was styled in a sleek low bun decorated with a white gajra. Nick Jonas complemented his wife's festive appearance in a cream-and-white embroidered kurta set. Their daughter Malti also joined the celebrations in a white lehenga, coordinating with her father's outfit. The photographs showed the family spending time together amid a festive setting decorated with candles, flowers and warm lights. One picture captured Priyanka and Nick with Malti, while another highlighted the detailed work on Priyanka's outfit. Nick responded to his wife's post with festive emojis, including a diya and a star-eyed face, adding to the family's Diwali wishes. ## Priyanka Continues to Celebrate Indian Festivals With Her Family Although Priyanka lives in the United States, she regularly celebrates Indian festivals and shares glimpses of these occasions with her followers. Her recent festive posts have highlighted her efforts to introduce Malti to Indian customs and traditions while growing up abroad. A few days earlier, Priyanka and Nick were also seen at a star-studded Diwali gathering in Los Angeles, according to reports. During the family's Dussehra celebrations in October, Priyanka shared photographs from a series of religious rituals at their Los Angeles home. The celebrations included Shivling Abhishek, a hawan and Kanya Pujan. One photograph showed Nick participating in the Kanya Pujan ritual by washing Malti's feet. Malti was dressed in an ivory outfit and wore a red scarf featuring the words "Jai Mata Di" during the Dussehra celebrations. The family also marked Karwa Chauth together in Los Angeles. Priyanka previously revealed that Nick had arranged his tour schedule to ensure he could be home for the occasion. She expressed her appreciation for his efforts and shared photographs from their celebration. ## Priyanka Chopra's Upcoming Film Projects On the professional front, Priyanka is preparing for her appearance in filmmaker SS Rajamouli's upcoming film Varanasi. The project stars Mahesh Babu and Prithviraj Sukumaran alongside Priyanka and is scheduled to release in theatres on April 7, 2027. She has also announced Ventilator 2 under her production banner, Purple Pebble Pictures. The upcoming film is a sequel to the 2016 Marathi movie Ventilator, which won three National Film Awards. Filmmaker Rajesh Mapuskar is returning as its writer and director, and the sequel is scheduled to release in 2027. While Priyanka continues to work on international and Indian projects, her latest Diwali photographs offered followers a personal glimpse into her celebrations with Nick and Malti, highlighting the family's festive traditions and time spent together. Sources: Priyanka Chopra's Instagram post and reports by IANS, WION, Free Press Journal, India.com, ANI and Outlook India.

title: Prerna Wanvari Challenges 'First Indian Presenter' Claim About Vijay Sethupathi at International Emmy Awards
description: Prerna Wanvari says Vijay Sethupathi is not the first Indian presenter at the International Emmys, recalling earlier appearances by Indian TV stars.
content: Actor Prerna Wanvari has challenged reports claiming that Tamil actor Vijay Sethupathi will become the first Indian to present an award at the International Emmy Awards. She has pointed out that several Indian television personalities had already appeared as presenters at the international ceremony years before his scheduled participation. Vijay Sethupathi is reportedly set to be one of the presenters at the 54th International Emmy Awards, which will take place in New York on November 23, 2026. The announcement generated excitement among his fans, with several reports describing his selection as a historic first for India. However, Prerna Wanvari questioned the accuracy of that description through a post on her Instagram Stories. Reacting to a report referring to Vijay as the first Indian presenter, she wrote, "You got this so wrong! And before me were two iconic women @aashkagoradia and @realsimonesingh who were first to present at The International Emmys in 2009 and 2010." Wanvari also shared a photograph of herself presenting an award at the International Emmy Awards in 2012, drawing attention to the earlier participation of Indian television personalities. ## Prerna Wanvari Recalls Earlier Indian Presenters According to Wanvari, Aashka Goradia and Simone Singh were the Indian presenters at the International Emmy Awards in 2009 and 2010 respectively. Wanvari herself presented the Arts Programming award at the 40th International Emmy Awards in 2012. She clarified that Vijay Sethupathi's participation at the upcoming ceremony is certainly worth celebrating, but said that calling him the first Indian presenter overlooked the contributions of those who had represented India before him. Her remarks have brought renewed attention to the earlier presence of Indian television actresses at the global awards ceremony. She argued that these appearances should also receive recognition rather than being overlooked while celebrating a new announcement. The discussion is not about questioning Vijay Sethupathi's selection as a presenter, but about ensuring that claims of a historic first accurately reflect the event's earlier history. Some reports have also noted that Priyanka Chopra presented at the Primetime Emmy Awards in Los Angeles in 2016. That is a separate ceremony from the International Emmy Awards, which honour television made outside the United States. ## Vijay Sethupathi to Present at the 54th International Emmy Awards Vijay Sethupathi's participation at the upcoming ceremony was first reported by The Hollywood Reporter India. The actor is expected to represent Indian entertainment as one of the presenters at the November 23 event in New York. The 54th International Emmy Awards will also feature Indian nominees in two categories. SonyLIV's series Real Kashmir Football Club has received a nomination in the Best Drama Series category, while comedian Vir Das's Netflix special Fool Volume is competing in the Best Comedy Series category. Vir Das previously hosted the International Emmy Awards in 2024, becoming the first Indian to do so, after winning the award for his comedy special Vir Das: Landing in 2023. The debate surrounding the presenter announcement has highlighted the importance of recognising earlier contributions by Indian television artists. While Vijay Sethupathi's upcoming appearance is attracting attention, Prerna Wanvari's intervention has reminded audiences that Indian performers have been part of the International Emmy stage for many years. Sources: Prerna Wanvari's Instagram Story and reports by WION, Sacnilk, Outlook India and The Hollywood Reporter India.

title: PM Modi Visits LK Advani on 99th Birthday as Veteran BJP Leader Enters His 100th Year
description: PM Modi visited veteran BJP leader LK Advani at his Delhi residence on his 99th birthday, as the BJP held a puja and havan at its headquarters.
content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi visited veteran Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader and former Deputy Prime Minister Lal Krishna Advani at his residence on Sunday, November 8, to extend birthday wishes as the senior leader entered the 100th year of his life. Advani turned 99 on the occasion, marking another milestone in his decades-long political journey. The visit was part of the birthday greetings extended to Advani by senior political leaders. Modi also shared a message on social media, describing November 8 as a landmark day and acknowledging the veteran leader's contribution to Indian politics and public life. In his message, the Prime Minister recalled Advani's journey from experiencing the Partition of India and rebuilding his life to strengthening the Bharatiya Jana Sangh and helping establish the BJP as a major political force. He also highlighted Advani's role during the Emergency, his leadership of the Somnath-to-Ayodhya Rath Yatra and his service in the Union government. Modi further referred to Advani's interests beyond politics, including his passion for reading, culture and cinema, as well as his work as an author. The Prime Minister also wrote an article reflecting on the veteran leader's life and contributions. ## BJP Organises Puja and Havan at Party Headquarters The BJP marked Advani's 99th birthday with a special puja and havan at its headquarters in New Delhi. The religious ceremony was held between 10 am and 10.30 am and was attended by senior party leaders, including BJP national president Nitin Nabin, and Advani's daughter, Pratibha Advani. The programme was organised to recognise Advani's long association with the party and his contribution to its organisational development. A video presentation of about 20 minutes, highlighting important moments from his political career and excerpts from his speeches, was also part of the birthday event. Nabin extended birthday wishes to Advani and described him as a source of inspiration for the party. He also acknowledged the veteran leader's role in the growth of the organisation and the Ram Janmabhoomi movement. Later in the day, Nabin also visited Advani's residence to personally convey his greetings, according to IANS. ## LK Advani's Political Journey Born on November 8, 1927, in Karachi, in present-day Pakistan, Lal Krishna Advani joined the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) in 1942. Following the Partition in 1947, he moved to India and went on to become one of the prominent figures in the Jana Sangh and the BJP. Advani served as BJP president for three terms between 1986 and 2005. His political journey included a central role in the party's expansion and the Somnath-to-Ayodhya Rath Yatra in 1990, an important episode in the history of the Ram Janmabhoomi movement. He later served as Union Home Minister and became India's Deputy Prime Minister from 2002 to 2004 during the government led by Atal Bihari Vajpayee. In recognition of his contribution to public life, he was conferred the Bharat Ratna in 2024. As Advani entered his 100th year, birthday greetings from the Prime Minister and other political leaders brought renewed attention to his long career in Indian politics and his role in the development of the BJP. Sources: reports by IANS, Outlook India, India TV, The Tribune and Organiser.

title: Karnataka CM DK Shivakumar and Daughter Aishwarya Face Backlash Over Remarks on Government School Teachers
description: Teachers' groups and educationists criticised remarks by Karnataka CM DK Shivakumar and his daughter Aishwarya about government school teachers.
content: Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar and his daughter, Aishwarya DKS Hegde, have drawn criticism from teachers' representatives, educationists and student groups over comments about the work of government school teachers. The row has also sharpened opposition to a state plan that invites private institutions and companies to adopt government schools. ## How the Row Began On November 4, Shivakumar appealed to private school managements to adopt government schools in rural areas or partner with the state in developing them. According to PTI, he suggested that private schools could send subject experts to government schools and pay their salaries, provide laboratory equipment and computers, and hand over buses to government school students instead of selling them. He added that institutions supporting a school would be allowed to add their own name to it. Reports mention a target of linking between 1,000 and 2,000 government schools with private institutions. The government has presented the plan as a way to improve the quality of rural education and reduce migration from villages to cities. Speaking about teacher pay, the Chief Minister said government school teachers earn between about ₹70,000 and ₹1.5 lakh a month. Later reports said he voiced disappointment about the commitment of some teachers drawing around ₹1.5 lakh, but clarified that he was not criticising the whole teaching community. ## Aishwarya Hegde's Remarks Aishwarya Hegde, trustee-secretary of the National Education Foundation, spoke at a corporate social responsibility (CSR) event organised by the state government. Her foundation supports the Karnataka Public School in Doddalahalli, and she used it as an example while discussing teacher accountability. "More than teacher shortage, low efficiency is the problem," she said. She claimed that some teachers earning around ₹1.1 lakh were not coming to school regularly, and argued that organisations investing in government schools should be able to check attendance and performance. ## Teachers' Representatives and Educationists Respond A.P. Ranganath, a Janata Dal (Secular) MLC for the Bangalore Teachers' Constituency, said the comments undermined the dignity of government school teachers, who are recruited through eligibility tests and competitive selection. He pointed out that teachers also handle many tasks outside the classroom, including supervising midday meals, distributing eggs, and taking part in census, caste and livestock surveys, electoral roll revision and election duty. Together with vacant posts and inadequate infrastructure, he said, these duties put heavy pressure on staff. Ranganath argued that private and government schools should not be judged by the same standards. "Private education may be a choice, but public education is a constitutional and social responsibility," he said. He asked Aishwarya to apologise to teachers and cited Articles 21A and 14 of the Constitution. Reports differ on whether his criticism was aimed only at her or at both her and her father. The Save Public Education Committee accused the government of shifting the blame for problems in public education onto teachers. It called the adoption plan "anti-people" and objected to private institutions attaching their names to adopted schools. A meeting organised by the committee drew former vice-chancellors A. Murigeppa and Sabiha Bhoomigowda, writers K. Marulasiddappa, S.G. Siddaramaiah, Roopa Hassan and Hema Pattanshetty, and educationist V.P. Niranjanaradhya. The All-India Democratic Students' Organisation demanded that the policy be withdrawn. The RTE Students Parents Association said that making sure government schools function properly is the state's responsibility, and the All Karnataka Pre-University Lecturers' Association president, A.H. Ningegowda, called for vacant teaching posts to be filled. Some commentators have described the plan as "backdoor privatisation", while the government presents it as a partnership. ## What the Debate Is About The dispute brings together several questions: how to ensure teacher accountability, how to fill vacancies, how to improve infrastructure, how many non-teaching duties teachers should carry, and what role private institutions and CSR money should play in public education. Supporters of the plan see extra resources and expertise for rural schools. Critics say voluntary contributions cannot replace the state's duty to run a well-staffed public school system. Sources: reports by Daily Pioneer, PTI (via The Week), Devdiscourse, Education Post and The Federal.

title: Ramayana Makers Issue Legal Notice Over Theatre Recordings, Warn of Criminal Action Citing Bombay High Court Orders
description: Ramayana: Part 1 makers warned against recording and sharing theatre footage, citing Bombay High Court orders of November 2 and 6, 2026.
content: The makers of Ramayana: Part 1 have warned cinema-goers that recording scenes inside theatres and sharing them online can lead to criminal, civil and contempt action. The warning, posted on the film's official social media accounts, cites two recent Bombay High Court orders that protect the film against unauthorised recording and circulation. According to the notice, the film's team had noticed footage from theatre screenings spreading across social media and messaging apps. It says the restrictions apply to everyone, including people who have not yet been identified, and asks those who have already posted clips to delete them. The makers said violators may face criminal, civil and contempt proceedings without any further notice, and that offending accounts and content will be reported to the authorities and the platforms concerned. The statement ends by reserving all of the production team's legal rights. ## What the Court Has Ordered The notice refers to orders dated November 2 and November 6, 2026, passed in Commercial IP Suit (L) No. 37230 of 2026. According to reports, the suit was filed by Godpower Media Private Limited, which is described as holding the copyright in the film. It claimed that some material, including trailers and unreleased footage, had already leaked online before the release. On November 2, Justice Madhav Jamdar granted a dynamic ad-interim injunction. It restrains unidentified "John Doe" persons and digital platforms from recording the film in theatres, or uploading, streaming or distributing the film or any portion of it without authorisation. A dynamic injunction generally allows the rights holder to act against new infringing links as they appear, without returning to court each time. On November 6, a day after the release, the court issued further directions after Godpower said pirated material had begun appearing online. Internet service providers and digital platforms must now remove pirated links within three hours of receiving a complaint from the copyright owner, and must share the contact details of nodal officers to handle such requests. The November 6 order is in addition to the November 2 injunction. The makers say that recording and sharing the film without permission amounts to copyright infringement and can attract criminal penalties, and that disobeying the court's directions can amount to contempt of court. ## About the Film Directed by Nitesh Tiwari, Ramayana: Part 1 was released worldwide on November 5, 2026, in Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam. It is produced by Namit Malhotra's Prime Focus Studios in association with DNEG and Yash's Monster Mind Creations. Ranbir Kapoor plays Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi plays Sita and Yash plays Ravana, with Ravie Dubey as Lakshman. The cast also includes Arun Govil, Vivek Oberoi, Lara Dutta, Kunal Kapoor, Rakul Preet Singh, Kajal Aggarwal and Indira Krishnan. An end-credit sequence teases Sunny Deol as Lord Hanuman and Raghav Juyal as Meghnad, and announces that Ramayana: Part 2 will release during Diwali 2028.
